skill.description: Swift development workflows for building, testing, formatting, signing, and deploying iOS and macOS apps with Xcode, SwiftPM, and simulator tools.
skill.summary: Build, test, format, sign, and troubleshoot Swift apps with focused Xcode and SwiftPM guidance.
skill.author: hmohamed01

security_audit.summary: The skill is a Swift developer workflow bundle with Markdown examples and local shell scripts. Most static detections are false positives from documentation examples, plist DOCTYPE URLs, and ordinary script checks. Confirmed risks remain around privileged Xcode or simulator commands, CI keychain handling, xargs filename handling, and an unconfirmed simulator reset action.

remediation.issue: Privileged Xcode and simulator commands are shown as normal workflow steps.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before sudo commands and document how to restore the previous Xcode selection or restart services safely.

remediation.issue: CI signing examples handle certificate files and keychain passwords.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance for secret storage, temporary keychain cleanup, and avoiding long-lived default keychains in CI jobs.

remediation.issue: The pre-commit hook passes git filenames through xargs without NUL-delimited handling.
remediation.suggestion: Use git diff -z and xargs -0 --, or a loop that preserves exact filenames and rejects unsafe paths.

remediation.issue: The simulator reset script erases all simulator data after only printing a warning.
remediation.suggestion: Add an interactive confirmation prompt or a required --yes flag before running xcrun simctl erase all.

content.user_title: Build Swift Apps With Xcode Workflows
content.value_statement: Swift projects require repeated build, test, signing, simulator, and package commands. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code focused Swift workflows and reusable scripts.
actual_capabilities: Guides Swift package and Xcode build or test commands using SwiftPM and xcodebuild.
Provides helper scripts for package creation, tests, formatting, linting, and simulator tasks.
Documents SwiftUI, concurrency, architecture, persistence, testing, SPM, code signing, and CI patterns.
Includes ExportOptions.plist and Package.swift templates for app distribution and package setup.
Points to Apple and GitHub Swift documentation for current API details.
limitations: Requires macOS and Xcode command line tools for most commands.
Does not include a complete sample app or production signing credentials.
Some troubleshooting examples can delete caches or simulator data and require user review.
Script behavior targets local developer projects, not hardened CI security controls.

use_cases.title: Create a Swift Package
use_cases.description: Generate a package structure with platform settings, formatting rules, lint settings, and standard source directories.

use_cases.title: Run iOS Project Tests
use_cases.description: Build and test Xcode projects or Swift packages with simulator destinations, coverage options, and readable output.

use_cases.title: Prepare CI and Signing Workflows
use_cases.description: Draft build pipelines, archive commands, ExportOptions files, and code signing steps for Apple platforms.

prompt_templates.title: Build My Package
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me build and test this Swift package. Explain each command before suggesting it.

prompt_templates.title: Create a New Package
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Swift library package named NetworkKit for iOS and macOS. Include formatting and linting setup.

prompt_templates.title: Debug Xcode Test Failures
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose these Xcode test failures and propose safe commands to rerun the tests with coverage.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Release Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a GitHub Actions workflow for archiving an iOS app, handling signing secrets, and exporting an IPA.

output_examples.input: Build and test a Swift package with coverage.
output_examples.output: A step-by-step test plan that checks Swift availability, runs the package tests, enables coverage, and explains where results appear.

output_examples.input: Prepare an iOS archive for App Store distribution.
output_examples.output: An archive checklist covering scheme selection, release configuration, signing requirements, export options, and verification steps.
A troubleshooting sequence that starts with listing devices and restarting services before recommending destructive simulator resets.

best_practices: Review every command before running it, especially commands using sudo, rm, or simulator erase actions.
Use project-specific schemes, destinations, and signing identities instead of placeholder values.
Run formatting and tests in check mode before applying automatic changes to a shared branch.
anti_patterns: Do not run destructive cleanup commands before confirming which files or simulator data will be removed.
Do not store certificate passwords, signing files, or API tokens directly in project files.
Do not copy CI examples into production without pinning tool versions and reviewing secret handling.

faq.question: Does this skill require Xcode?
faq.answer: Yes. Most workflows require macOS with Xcode or Xcode Command Line Tools installed.

faq.question: Can it create a complete iOS app?
faq.answer: It provides workflows and templates, but it does not include a full production app template.

faq.question: Does it support Swift Package Manager?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes package creation, build, test, dependency, and local package guidance.

faq.question: Can it manage iOS simulators?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes simulator listing, booting, installing, launching, screenshots, and appearance commands.

faq.question: Does it handle app signing?
faq.answer: It documents signing commands, ExportOptions templates, and CI keychain setup patterns.

faq.question: Is it safe to run all troubleshooting commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. Commands that use sudo, rm, or simulator erase actions need explicit review first.
